## Incident Report: PCAP Forensic Analysis — 2024-11-26 Traffic Analysis Exercise

### Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.11.26.183 | Consistent source of all malicious traffic |
| MAC | d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b | Ethernet layer, ARP exchange with gateway/DC 10.11.26.3 (00:24:e8:7f:09:5d) |
| Hostname | DESKTOP-B8TQK49 | NBNS name registration (`<00>` Workstation, `<20>` Server service) from 10.11.26.183 |
| Domain | NEMOTODES / nemotoads.health | NBNS domain broadcasts, DNS queries to `NEMOTODES-DC.nemotoads.health` |
| Logged-in user | **oboomwald** | Kerberos `CNameString` observed in traffic both from 10.11.26.183 and the DC (10.11.26.3) |

Domain controller/DNS server for the LAN: 10.11.26.3 (NEMOTODES-DC).

### Malware Family
**NetSupport RAT** (commercial remote-admin tool NetSupport Manager, abused as a RAT/trojan) — **signature-confirmed**.

Evidence:
- Suricata/ET alerts fired directly on the traffic: `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin`, `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Response`, `ET POLICY NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`.
- Client HTTP `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` observed in every POST to the C2.
- Beacon behavior confirmed in raw traffic: repeated `POST /fakeurl.htm HTTP/1.1` (plaintext HTTP, not TLS, despite using dst port 443) to 194.180.191.64, `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, roughly every 60 seconds — the classic NetSupport client check-in pattern.
- A DNS lookup and HTTP GET to `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` (`/location/loca.asp`) immediately followed the first C2 checkin — NetSupport's legitimate geolocation service, which the RAT client also queries on startup.

### Delivery Chain
1. 04:50:14–04:50:40 UTC — victim resolves `modandcrackedapk.com` (flagged by ET as a "ZPHP" cluster domain, a known cracked-software/mod lure category) and establishes a TLS session to 193.42.38.139 with SNI `modandcrackedapk.com`.
2. 04:50:45 UTC — within 5 seconds of the last packet to that site, the host initiates the first connection to 194.180.191.64:443 and performs the NetSupport RAT C2 checkin and geolocation lookup.
3. From that point on, the infected host beacons to 194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm roughly once per minute for the rest of the capture (two separate TCP sessions logged, spanning ~48 minutes and ~3 minutes respectively).

The actual payload/binary transfer occurred inside the encrypted TLS session to 193.42.38.139, so no file name or hash for the dropped NetSupport client is recoverable from this capture — HTTP export of objects only yielded the plaintext C2 checkin bodies (`fakeurl.htm`) and unrelated benign downloads (Windows CTL updates, Adobe telemetry, NCSI test).

### IOCs Grounded in the Capture

**C2 endpoints:**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — NetSupport RAT C2, POST beacon to `/fakeurl.htm`, confirmed by ETPRO CnC signatures.

**Domains:**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` — resolves to 193.42.38.139; delivery/lure site, flagged by ET as ZPHP domain in DNS lookup and TLS SNI.
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` — resolves to 104.26.1.231; NetSupport RAT's geolocation lookup endpoint (legitimate NetSupport infrastructure abused by the RAT client).

**URLs:**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` — C2 checkin URI, repeated POSTs with `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`.
- `http://104.26.1.231/location/loca.asp` — NetSupport GeoLocation lookup request.

**File names / hashes:** None recoverable. The payload delivery occurred over TLS to 193.42.38.139 (encrypted); no plaintext executable transfer or file object was observed anywhere in the capture.

### Benign Context (not IOCs)
- `10.11.26.183 -> 104.117.247.184` (msftconnecttest.com), `104.117.247.99` (r10.o.lencr.org, CRL check), `23.53.127.200` (ctldl.windowsupdate.com), `acroipm2.adobe.com`, `classicgrand.com`, `confirmsubscription.com`, and the entire Microsoft/MSN/Office/Bing/Google telemetry set — standard Windows/browser/OS background noise, not attacker infrastructure.
- The SMB/EFSR alerts (`ETPRO POLICY [MS-EFSR]...`, `ET INFO Potentially unsafe SMBv1...`, `GPL NETBIOS SMB...NTLMSSP...overflow`, `GPL NETBIOS SMB...DOS Attempt`) are victim-to-DC (10.11.26.183 -> 10.11.26.3) traffic on ports 139/445. These are aged GPL signatures that commonly false-positive on normal Windows NTLMSSP/SMB session negotiation and EFSRPC calls during routine domain logon; nothing in this traffic ties them to the NetSupport RAT activity, and no lateral-movement payload was observed. Treated as context, not confirmed malicious activity.

### Incident Summary
The Windows workstation DESKTOP-B8TQK49 (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged on as domain user **oboomwald** in the NEMOTODES/nemotoads.health domain, visited the cracked-software lure site `modandcrackedapk.com` and, within seconds, began communicating with a NetSupport RAT command-and-control server at 194.180.191.64:443 using the NetSupport Manager client, confirmed by multiple ETPRO/ET Suricata signatures for NetSupport RAT CnC activity. The host continued to beacon to the C2 every ~60 seconds for the remainder of the capture, with a supporting geolocation lookup to NetSupport's own infrastructure — consistent with a fake-software/cracked-app malvertising delivery of a NetSupport RAT (RAT-as-a-service) infection.
